clue.text: Agreement to this form was the householder's duty, *we hear

indicators.note: the clue tells us the words it describes are to be taken as spoken, so their sound gives the spelling

parts.words: to this form was the householder's duty
parts.note: the householder had to con (study and fill in) the census form, so these words describe the phrase con census

explanation.surface: A remark that filling in the national survey form was a duty of every head of household.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'con' is an old word for to study; the census form had to be conned, and 'con census' said out loud matches the word for general agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: General accord among a group is a consensus.

clue.text: Material for the managers of a potato-frying business ?

definitions.text: the managers of a potato-frying business

explanation.surface: A question about what to make of the directors of a chip shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' links two senses: a building board of compressed wood chips, and the board of directors of a chip firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Compressed wood fragments make a sheet building material, and a company running a chip shop would have a governing board.

clue.text: Approaches a saner representation

indicators.note: a representation presents the same letters in a new form

explanation.surface: Someone approaches with a more reasonable portrayal.
explanation.definitionFit: To come closer to something is to near it.

clue.text: Always that bit extra, always

parts.note: ever means always
more means an additional amount

explanation.surface: A repeated insistence on always giving a little more.
explanation.definitionFit: Forever, for all time, is the poetic evermore.

clue.text: The Flying Doctor's spiritual counterpart ?

parts.note: the airborne medic heals the body, so his opposite number for the soul is a clergyman, slang naming him the guide of the heavens

explanation.walkthrough: The Flying Doctor is Australia's airborne medical service; a sky pilot is slang for a chaplain or clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman, especially a forces chaplain, is slangily a sky pilot, guiding souls heavenward.

clue.text: Hostile encounters piecemeal

explanation.surface: Fights breaking out bit by bit.
explanation.definitionFit: Fights are scraps, and so are small leftover pieces, which is what piecemeal suggests.

clue.text: Does it call for a costume ornament ?

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether an outfit demands a decorative trimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' joins the two senses: a horn that sounds a military call, and a tube-shaped glass bead sewn on dresses.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass horn sounds the reveille call, and a small tubular bead used to trim clothing shares the same name.

clue.text: When driving does he give supporting signals?

definitions.text: When driving does he give supporting signals?

parts.words: When driving does he give supporting signals
parts.note: a motorist signals before reversing, and a supporter who gives signals of support has done the same verb

explanation.walkthrough: Reversing a car is backing it; giving support is also backing. The clue asks about both.
explanation.definitionFit: Both reversing and supporting are expressed by the same past tense of the verb to back.

clue.text: Statesman who had it in the bag ?'

definitions.text: Statesman who had it in the bag ?'

parts.words: Statesman who had it in the bag
parts.note: a Victorian prime minister gave his name to a hinged leather travelling bag, so his name is in the bag

explanation.walkthrough: William Gladstone, four times British prime minister, gave his name to the Gladstone bag.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian Liberal prime minister's surname also names a type of hinged luggage.

clue.text: It's all over a point in the revised deed

indicators.note: in puts the compass point inside the reworked letters
revised says the letters of the word deed are reordered

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A revised legal deed with a point inserted means the matter is closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges DEED and N goes in it; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: When something has finished, it has come to its close.

clue.text: Mind the pictures !

parts.note: read as a warning to be careful near the paintings, but meaning the pictures formed in the mind

explanation.definitionFit: Mental images collectively, the pictures the mind forms, make up a writer's or thinker's imagery.

clue.text: The defendant, Mr. Roe

parts.note: in old English law the fictitious defendant in an action of ejectment was called Roe, with a stock first name

explanation.walkthrough: John Doe and Richard Roe were the made-up plaintiff and defendant of old English property lawsuits.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal fiction named its imaginary defendant Richard Roe, so his first name completes the phrase.

clue.text: Slatternly woman employed for sweeping

explanation.surface: A slovenly woman taken on as a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is dialect for a slovenly woman, and also a broom made of twigs bound to a handle.

clue.text: Half-back had reporters in, and got good notices no doubt

indicators.note: in shows the reporters are placed inside the turned word for half
back tells us the word for half is turned round, read from its end to its start

parts.note: demi- is a prefix meaning half
the press is a collective name for journalists

explanation.surface: A football half-back let journalists in and was surely rewarded with glowing match reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-back' looks like a football position; 'back' turns DEMI into IMED, and PRESS goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: One who has got favourable reviews has made a good impression, having impressed the critics.

clue.text: Where one waits for Ena with a motor perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of the name and the vehicle might be arranged in another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sits waiting for a woman called Ena to arrive with her car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ENA and MOTOR; 'for' and 'with a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A small waiting room before a main chamber is an anteroom.

clue.text: They have to make outs in this business

definitions.text: They have to make outs in this business

parts.words: They have to make outs in this business
parts.note: read as the trade where workers must make cuts, the cutting of cloth for suits

explanation.walkthrough: 'outs' is the page's misprint for 'cuts': a tailor's work is cutting cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The trade of making suits and fitted clothes is tailoring.

clue.text: The hollow sound of success in business ?

explanation.surface: A question about the echo of a thriving trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep resonant noise is a boom, and so is a period of rapid economic growth.

clue.text: Where, in Notts, English women cannot compete on 'equal terms?

definitions.text: Where, in Notts, English women cannot compete on 'equal terms?

parts.words: Where, in Notts, English women cannot compete on 'equal terms
parts.note: a town in Nottinghamshire whose name, split

explanation.walkthrough: Notts is Nottinghamshire, an English county; the town of Mansfield there splits into man's field.
explanation.definitionFit: Mansfield is a market town in Nottinghamshire whose name reads as man's field.

clue.text: Poet would be more amusing without a letter on tap

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the word for more amusing sits round the letter

parts.note: wittier means funnier
H marks the hot tap

explanation.surface: A poet would be funnier if he dropped a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: WITTIER goes round H. The surface reads it as 'lacking'. John Greenleaf Whittier was an American poet.
explanation.definitionFit: John Greenleaf Whittier was a nineteenth-century American Quaker poet.

clue.text: Useful for cracking the surface before a dip at breakfast-time

definitions.text: Useful for cracking the surface before a dip at breakfast-time

parts.words: Useful for cracking the surface before a dip at breakfast-time
parts.note: sounds like breaking ice for a morning swim, but describes the small utensil that taps open a boiled shell before dipping

explanation.definitionFit: A small spoon for eating boiled eggs is used to crack the shell and dip in.

clue.text: The Prosecutor is on the platform

parts.note: DA is District Attorney, the American public prosecutor

explanation.surface: The prosecuting lawyer has stepped up on to the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised stand at one end of a hall is a dais.

clue.text: Mortification, say, when leather's untanned

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the word for mortification aloud and spell what we hear differently

parts.note: chagrin is vexation or mortification

explanation.surface: Someone is humiliated to find their leather has not been tanned.
explanation.walkthrough: Shagreen is rough untanned hide, often of shark or horse; it is pronounced like chagrin.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw granulated hide, untanned leather, is called shagreen.

clue.text: Reviler who hits the roof!

explanation.surface: A critic who loses their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: One who slates, criticises harshly, is a slater, as is a tradesman hammering tiles on a roof.

clue.text: Jack and Bill meet us at' the counter

parts.note: an AB, able seaman, is a sailor, and jack is slang for a sailor
AC is short for account, a bill
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two men named Jack and Bill meet us at the shop counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of beads on wires used for counting is a counter.

clue.text: Jail, taking a £1 wager? That's the argument

parts.note: quod is old British slang for prison
L is the abbreviation for pound (from libra) and I is the Roman numeral one
a bet is a wager

explanation.surface: A prisoner places a one-pound bet, and that is the point of debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking a' is a link; £1 gives L for the pound and I for one. A quodlibet is a subtle point of scholastic debate.
explanation.definitionFit: A quodlibet is a philosophical or theological question set for debate, a disputation.

clue.text: Sheets of paper for church singers, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the singers' word is spoken and we spell what is heard

parts.note: a choir sings in church

explanation.surface: A request for paper music sheets for the church singers.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty-four or twenty-five sheets of paper make a quire.

clue.text: Works return of bogus cards?

indicators.note: return means the word for musical works is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: ops is short for opera, plural of opus, a composer's works
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether some works are a return on a pack of fake playing cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns OPS into SPO and adds OF. Spoof began as a hoaxing game invented by the comedian Arthur Roberts, hence bogus cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoax or parody is a spoof, the name of a nonsense game of trickery.

clue.text: The shape of 18's target

parts.note: the breakfast spoon is aimed at a boiled egg, so this asks for the egg's outline

explanation.definitionFit: Egg-shaped solids are ovoid.

clue.text: Second way the law appeared to Mr. Bumble

definitions.text: Second way the law appeared to Mr. Bumble

parts.words: Second way the law appeared to Mr. Bumble
parts.note: in Oliver Twist the beadle Mr Bumble says the law is a ass, and then calls it a idiot, the second description

explanation.walkthrough: Mr Bumble, the beadle in Dickens's Oliver Twist, declares 'the law is a ass, a idiot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling the law an idiot means judging it foolish, so the adjective is the second verdict.

clue.text: Pies too can make an atom of difference

indicators.note: can make says these letters may be reworked into a new word

explanation.surface: A claim that a couple of pies can make all the difference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pies too' rearranges; 'an atom of difference' plays on 'a lot of difference'.
explanation.definitionFit: Atoms of one element that differ in neutron number are its isotopes.

clue.text: Composer of study from The Spanish Garden?

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the

indicators.note: from shows the word for a study is taken away from the garden

parts.note: a den is a private study

explanation.surface: A question about who composed a study inspired by a garden in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' looks like a musical piece; it is DEN, removed from GARDEN to leave GAR after EL.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Elgar was the English composer of the Enigma Variations.

clue.text: Played to the balcony ?

parts.note: suggests an actor playing to the upper seats of a theatre, but means a suitor making music beneath a lady's window

explanation.definitionFit: A lover singing or playing beneath a window at night has sung a love song to her.
